newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says French textile aid illegal, delays ruling.
newsitem.headline: EU says French textile aid illegal, delays ruling.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday French plans to help the country's textile industry stimulate job creation were illegal but delayed a formal decision for two weeks.

"The European Commission concluded today that the French textile plan is, in its current form, incompatible with European rules on state aid," Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said in a statement. "At my suggestion, the Commission delayed its formal decision by two weeks."
French Employment Minister Jacques Barrot would come to Brussels on Friday to discuss how to change the plan to make it respect EU rules, Van Miert said.

The Commission has consistently said it will not tolerate sectoral aid because it distorts competition in the EU's border-free market and three months ago ordered Belgium to scrap a scheme designed to support export-led companies which have been hit by a stronger Belgian franc.
In October it openly questioned the French measures which were expected to save the textile industry 2.1 billion francs in salary-linked social security contributions.
